messages:
maria: AM check-in — landed PR #4821 that adds async batch-splitting for long sequences. Ran a quick perf suite against master: p95 token latency down ~8%, cost/tok improvement ~4%. Pushed canary image to staging.

maria: Blocker — KV warmup spike on shard-12 when qps dips below 4rps, causes short tail latency. I tried increasing `kv.prefetch_threshold` to 0.2 but saw evictions still spike. Repro steps below.

maria: Repro:
```
heyload --target staging-shard-12 --qps 2 --seq-len 1024 --duration 300
```

alex: Nice! I can look into the shard heatmap. Quick Q: did you run with `--kv-ttl=60`? That changes eviction behavior.

maria: nope, default ttl. Can try. Also logs attached in gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/kvs-warm-spike

chen: pinging @jamal — he touched eviction heuristics last week. Jamal any ideas? :eyes:

jamal: saw similar on Tuesday in perf run. Hypothesis: the prefetcher threshold uses a global slot metric that undercounts when batch slotting reassigns. I'll dig in tonight. Could you include the `slot_map` snapshot? (`/debug/slot_map`)

maria: added slot_map snapshot to gist.

ops-bot: Deploy started for image redwood/runtime-canary:sha-ab12 -> staging (canary=10%) :rocket:

alex: small nit — for better comparison include p50/p95/p99 from the benchmark; p99 is more sensitive to warmups.

maria: good call, I'll rerun with 30min warmup and capture p99. ETA ~2h. If anyone else is free, a quick review of PR #4821 would help (esp. splitting logic in kernel/slot_allocator.go).

chen: can review later today. :+1:

jamal: I'll reproduce locally tomorrow morning and test with a long-tail workload. If I find a fix I'll post a patch to the prefetcher config.

maria: thanks team — will follow up with results in this thread. Anyone else with context feel free to jump in. :slightly_smiling_face:
